rationale: M14 IMPORTS_ENUM gaps 3 and 4. Two type POSITIONS that name a type and published nothing. (3) A type PREDICATE: measured on the pinned wasm, the return type of `f(): x is Foo` is NOT a type_annotation — it is `(return_type (type_predicate_annotation (type_predicate name: (identifier) type: (type_identifier))))` — so extractDeclaredTypeRefs' type_annotation case never fired for that shape and `function g(x: unknown): x is Foo` published NO relationship at all. `asserts x is Foo` is the same idea two hops down (asserts_annotation > asserts > type_predicate). (4) A type-parameter CONSTRAINT: `<T extends C>` cannot be checked without C, and the declaration is the only place C is named; `(type_parameter name: (type_identifier) constraint: (constraint (type_identifier)))` had no case, so `function f<T extends C>()` published `references f -> T` — the BINDING — and never C. Corpus draw over tracked .ts files of bb_tests/repositories/typescript: 53 constraint sites in the first 40 files, 13 of 24 distinct names reached by an edge; after the fix 24 of 24. THE FORBIDS CARRY THE RULE: the predicate's `name` (`x`) is a parameter binding and the type parameter's own `name` (`T`) is a binding, and the java oracle states it in its own words — 'a TYPE PARAMETER DECLARATION is not a type usage: <T>, <A extends B>, <K, V> declare variables, they do not name a type in the file'. An intersection constraint contributes BOTH names (onlyNamed), which is pinned because a collector that took only the first named child would drop one silently. An interface owner gets a reference row and NO uses row — the reference pass's owner list does not include interfaces — and that asymmetry is pinned so it is visible rather than mistaken for a missing edge.

THE POSITION PIN, in the negative. A type predicate is not an ordinary annotation: if the gain above were really the pre-existing declared_type surface firing on some other node, this row would match and the fixture would fail. `meta.relationshipType: null` is the runner's ABSENT convention, so a row that pinned the wrong position could not pass either.

THE FABRICATION THIS FIXTURE EXISTS TO CATCH, pinned by POSITION as well as by endpoint. The java oracle states the rule in its own words: 'a TYPE PARAMETER DECLARATION is not a type usage: <T>, <A extends B>, <K, V> declare variables, they do not name a type in the file'. Pinning the position as well as the endpoint is what makes this row catch the collector that leaks the binding at the DECLARATION while a legitimate `Q` usage elsewhere would still pass.
